Patient demographics:
  age: 21
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: African
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Surgeon
  trauma_type: Natural disaster
  pcl5: 55

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Trauma-Related Events: Trauma-related events, Weather Similarity: Similar weather conditions to when the event happened, Nighttime/Dark: Night-time or waking up in the dark
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Exercise: Exercise, Emotion Control: I try hard to control my emotions, Fawn Response: become overly compliant when feeling threatened
  Threat: Startle to Sounds: I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people, Physical Reactivity: Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience, Hypervigilance: Being superalert or watchful or on guard
  Negative Appraisals: Life Destroyed: My life has been destroyed by the trauma, Can't Rely on Self: I can't rely on myself, Helplessness: I can't stop bad things from happening to me

Vignette:
Evelyn, a 21-year-old African-American woman and aspiring surgeon, had always been driven by her passion for saving lives. Growing up in Houston, she had witnessed several natural disasters but was particularly impacted by the devastating hurricane that hit during her senior year of high school. The event left an indelible mark on her psyche, reshaping her world in profound ways. The hurricane struck with such ferocity that Evelyn vividly remembers the howling winds and relentless rain pounding against the walls of her home. As she huddled with her family in the sheltered basement, power outages plunged them into darkness, and every creak or groan of the building was a stark reminder of their vulnerability. The night seemed endless, punctuated only by sporadic lightning that illuminated the chaos outside. This experience has since become deeply embedded in her psyche, particularly triggering her during similar weather conditions. Since then, Evelyn’s life has been irrevocably altered. Nighttime and darkness evoke intense anxiety, as she relives those terrifying hours spent waiting for the storm to pass. The dark brings back memories of the hurricane's fury, leaving her feeling helpless and exposed. She struggles with the idea that her life has been destroyed by this trauma, believing that it has fundamentally changed her ability to trust herself or her surroundings. Evelyn’s daily routine as a surgeon is fraught with triggers and challenges. Her hypervigilance makes it nearly impossible for her to relax, even in the controlled environment of the hospital. She remains on high alert at all times, scanning her surroundings for any potential threats. This heightened state of arousal often leads to startling reactions at ordinary sounds, such as doors slamming or equipment beeping. The physical reactivity is especially pronounced when she encounters conditions reminiscent of the hurricane—darkness and wind can send her into a panic. To cope with these overwhelming feelings, Evelyn has developed maladaptive strategies that have become habitual over time. She avoids exercise, believing it might exacerbate her anxiety. Instead, she focuses on controlling her emotions, often suppressing any signs of distress in professional settings to maintain composure. In moments of stress or perceived threat, she tends to fawn, becoming overly compliant and deferential to those around her—a behavior that has strained some of her relationships at work. Her hypervigilance and avoidance have taken a toll on both her personal life and career. Colleagues have noticed her increasingly rigid demeanor and the lengths she goes to avoid certain tasks or situations that remind her of the hurricane. This has led to a sense of isolation, as she feels she cannot rely on herself or others in times of need. Her belief that "I can’t stop bad things from happening" further fuels this anxiety, making it difficult for her to engage fully with colleagues and patients. Despite these challenges, Evelyn’s underlying hope is to regain control over her life and return to the level of confidence she once had as a surgeon. The cumulative effects of her symptoms have finally pushed her to seek help. She recognizes that her current state has reached a point where it no longer aligns with her professional aspirations or personal well-being. What frightens her most is the fear of being forever defined by this traumatic event, but what she hopes for is the possibility of reclaiming her life and finding a way to integrate these experiences without them dictating every aspect of who she is. Evelyn’s journey towards recovery begins with acknowledging the profound impact of the hurricane on her psyche and understanding that healing is possible through professional support. She seeks help not just to manage her symptoms, but to rebuild her sense of self and restore a life enriched by hope and resilience.
